{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the tail of the fish, the forked end that makes the outline read as a fish and not just an oval. I laid roughly 30 dominoes across both tail pieces, starting early so they were standing and waiting when the body lines arrived. The start domino reached about 121 of the 129 standing dominoes, and the bottom tail was carried by the run.

Execution: I worked the fiddly part of the job, the tail pieces and their joins. I laid the tail strokes a hand's width short of the body lines, as the technique requires, so I didn't knock anyone's work. I then inspected the tail area closely several times, at about 2:15 through 5:00, to find where the chain was and wasn't connecting. That gave the table accurate information for the top-tail repair. After the repair I checked the run from the nose again and confirmed it was connected through the body and both tail pieces.

Collaboration: I told the table early which pieces I had already started, so nobody doubled up on the bottom tail. When Maya took on redoing the top tail, I dropped my own connect so we wouldn't collide, and I stayed clear afterwards. I kept my hands off the finished fish in the last minutes so nobody risked a bump.

Leadership: I took ownership of a defined piece of the picture, the tails, and kept it clear who was doing what. I made the call to step back when stepping in would have caused conflict, and I held to the hands-off rule once the run was verified. I think my share of the table's result was about 25 percent: the tail work, the inspections, and the final check.", "my_share_percent": 25}
